title: Neuropsychology & Cognitive Function
summary: Neuropsychology: brain-behavior relationships, neuropsychological assessment, brain lobes, executive functions, neuroplasticity, and cognitive function.
objectives: Identify brain lobes and their functions.
revision: Neuropsychology: brain-behavior relationships, brain lobes, executive functions, neuroplasticity, cognitive function.
traps: Brain lobes: frontal (executive), parietal (sensory), temporal (auditory/memory), occipital (visual).

notes.t: The study of the relationship between brain function and behavior, including how brain injury and neurological conditions affect cognition and emotion.

i: Frontal lobe: executive function, planning, decision-making, personality
Parietal lobe: sensory processing, spatial awareness
Temporal lobe: auditory processing, memory, language

notes.t: The brain's capacity to reorganize itself by forming new neural connections throughout life in response to experience and learning.

i: Working memory, cognitive flexibility, inhibitory control

notes.t: UGC NET may ask about brain lobes, neuropsychological assessment, and neuroplasticity.

mnemonics.title: FNPE
mnemonics.text: F — Frontal lobe (executive), P — Parietal lobe (sensory/spatial), N — Temporal lobe (auditory/memory), E — Occipital lobe (visual)

flashcards.a: Brain's ability to reorganize through experience.
